messages:
alec: Heads-up — customer ticket flagged missing actor info on audit events for KMS decrypts. Two different customers, both saying UI shows no email or name for decrypt actions.
sec-bot: alert: audit-collector noticed 1.2% of events with dropped_fields during ingest. sample: https://logs.internal/reports/1955 — rule: dropped_fields > 1%
maya: can you paste an example event id so we can trace the pipeline?
alec: sure, here's the raw event we pulled from s3 (sanitized):
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_20260318_01",
  "ts": "2026-03-18T15:12:03Z",
  "action": "kms.decrypt",
  "resource": "customer-a:v1/key-abc",
  "principal": {
    "principal_id": "okta|12345",
    "principal_type": "user",
    "email": null,
    "display_name": null
  },
  "auth_type": "sso",
  "ingest_pipeline": "audit-v2"
}
```
alec: note: principal_id is present (okta) but email/display_name are null. This is what makes UI show empty actor.
dmitri: iirc we added a claim-filter step during the oauth migrator rollout last month — possible it dropped non-standard claims when provider didn't include email. grep suggestion: `rg "claim-filter|oauth-migrator" --stats` in infra repo.
ryan: is this only on Private customers or seen in Hosted as well?
alec: seen in Hosted and Private. Both customers are Hosted but we have one Private report coming in that's likely related.
maya: immediate question: for customer-facing audit events we should never show blank actor. two quick mitigations: (1) UI fallback to display principal_id when email missing; (2) ingester validation rule to flag/reject events missing any of [principal_id, principal_type] or at least add fallback metadata field `actor_representation`. Thoughts?
dmitri: agree on both. cheap fix — UI fallback to `principal_id` or `okta|<id>` is low risk. For longer term, fix migrator to preserve `email` claim if present and stop normalizing away `display_name`.
sec-bot: audit-ingester-bot: new check registered: REQUIRE(actor.principal_id) for customer-visible events. will start dropping to quarantine/notify in 5m for testing.
maya: i'll take ownership of the backfill/backfill validation — i'll run a query for events where `action:kms.decrypt` and `principal.email:null` and produce a CSV for customers. estimating ~12k events across last 90 days.
alec: thanks. for customer comms: recommend short note explaining we found incomplete actor metadata in some decrypt events, we will backfill display with principal_id and offer direct csv export of affected events.
dry: (reaction) :eyes:
dmitri: patch plan: 1) revert/mend claim-filter rule in oauth-migrator (PR), 2) add ingest-time enrichment (copy principal_id -> actor_representation if email missing), 3) backfill script to populate actor_representation for past events. I'll open PRs today.
ryan: SLA/incident? does this require Sev? customers got confused but no security exposure seen so far.
maya: not a security breach but data quality incident. i'll log an internal incident ticket for tracking and customer comms.
alec: ok — action items: maya = customer comms + backfill, dmitri = migrator patch + ingest enrichment, sec-bot/audit-ingester-bot = quarantine rule enabled, ryan = coordinate if customer needs escalation.
alec: thanks all. will post a short runbook in the incident tracker and ping legal if customers request formal attestation. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: noted. continuing monitor, will post summary in #incidents when backfill completes.
